summary: You spend most of the game routing a rondel-like path north to south, deciding when to spend actions upgrading your cattle, buildings, and railroad workers versus rushing herds to Kansas City for delivery bonuses. It rewards long-term engine building over multiple deliveries rather than any single big score.
praised: Tight, interlocking engine-building with multiple viable strategies
High replayability from variable building setup and station tiles
Satisfying tension between short-term cash needs and long-term engine investment
Strong player agency with few wasted turns
criticised: Steep rules overhead and long first play for new groups
Some luck/timing dependency on which buildings appear along the trail
Can run long at higher player counts, with downtime between turns
Kansas City auction/bonus spaces can feel swingy

interaction.kind: spatial blocking on the trail and building slots, indirect competition for scoring bonuses

scoring.why: Points accumulate from cattle delivered, buildings built, railroad progress, objective cards, and station bonuses, so the winner is whoever best balances several engines rather than maxing one
